scope.comparison_kind: ES5-compatible constructs versus ES12 constructs in the same ES12-capable runtime
scope.warning: These results do not compare an ES5-mode runtime with an ES12-mode runtime and do not measure global-scope transpilation. Do not infer ES5-runtime or global-scope performance.

method.caller_context: Scoped application configured with js_level=es_latest; global.UsefulStuff is a dependency invoked by the scoped benchmark script.
method.execution_order: fixed in the order represented by the source script
notes: Each reported mean is total elapsed milliseconds divided by 10000 iterations.
The two supplied runs are retained for auditability.
Very short benchmarks are sensitive to timer granularity and harness overhead.
No statistical significance claim is available from two runs.

ratio_semantics.formula: candidate average mean milliseconds / baseline average mean milliseconds
ratio_semantics.interpretation: Above 1 means the candidate was slower; below 1 means the candidate was faster.

comparisons.workload: Sum a newly allocated five-element array through forEach.

observed.claim: The traditional callback averaged 10.31% less time than the arrow callback in this exact two-run workload.

limitations: Array allocation and forEach overhead are included.

baseline.label: Direct property access
baseline.operation: total += obj.a; total += obj.b; total += obj.c

candidate.label: Destructuring
candidate.operation: var {a, b, c} = obj; total += a; total += b; total += c

comparisons.workload: Read three properties from one preallocated object and sum them.

observed.claim: Direct property access averaged 16.67% less time than destructuring in this exact two-run workload.

limitations: Totals of 17-21 ms make timer granularity material.

baseline.label: Classic for loop
baseline.operation: for (var i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) { sum += arr[i]; }

candidate.label: for...of
candidate.operation: for (const value of arr) { sum += value; }

comparisons.workload: Sum 100 numeric elements from one preallocated array.

observed.claim: for...of averaged 4.52 times the duration of the classic indexed loop in this exact two-run workload.

limitations: Only dense numeric arrays of length 100 were measured.

baseline.label: for sum
baseline.operation: for (var i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) { sum += arr[i]; }

comparisons.workload: Sum 100 numeric elements from one preallocated array.

observed.claim: reduce averaged 10.41% less time than the classic indexed loop across the two supplied runs, but the per-run advantage varied substantially.

limitations: The candidate advantage was 18.83% in run 1 and 1.68% in run 2.
Only dense numeric arrays of length 100 were measured.

comparisons.workload: Build a 50-element array from empty; spread reallocates the growing array on every append.

observed.claim: Repeated spread append averaged 27.52 times the duration of push in this exact two-run workload.

limitations: This measures repeated copying through spread, not one spread operation or bulk concatenation.

comparisons.workload: Read 1000 existing string keys from prepopulated Object and Map containers and sum numeric values.

observed.claim: Map.get averaged 39.75% more time than object property lookup in this exact two-run workload.

limitations: Only 1000 existing string keys with numeric values were measured.
The dynamic key-string expression is included in both variants.

comparisons.workload: Construct one short string containing one numeric interpolation.

observed.claim: The template literal averaged 3.58 times the duration of concatenation in this exact two-run workload.

limitations: Totals of 9-36 ms make timer granularity and harness overhead material.
Only one short constant-heavy string shape was measured.
